label: negative
description: sweep() drops nonReentrant and even writes state (collected -= amount) AFTER the external call, so CEI is deliberately NOT the reason it is safe. The only external call target is `treasury`, an immutable address fixed in the constructor to a known-trusted contract.
why_labeled: Exclusion 2.3: the sole external-call callee is an immutable/constant trusted address set at construction, so an attacker cannot substitute a malicious contract to re-enter through. CEI is violated here on purpose (the state write follows the call) precisely to isolate 2.3 as the operative exclusion rather than 2.2 — if the rule leaned on ordering it would fire; it must instead recognise the immutable trusted callee and stay quiet.
